searchText: As a dev, this is basically how rollouts go .All the action is in the beginning. By the time you're ready to roll out to Prod, it's just going through the motions That is how *good* rollouts go. Plenty of companies rollout prematurely with lots of action at deploy time. Not always to the fault of engineers though, so much grief due to corporate/management pushing with unrealistic timelines what are `totalDifficulty` and `difficulty` of a block going to represent post merge? `difficulty` will be `0`. `totalDifficulty` I guess will just stagnate at the `totalDifficulty` of the last block? Maybe some clients will remove it from the JSON-RPC response? We historically have been pretty bad about defining JSON-RPC behavior with hard forks that change them. 😖 is there a spec for JSON-RPC post merge? There is no spec for JSON-RPC pre-merge. 😬 Well, there is a bunch of partial ones, but all of them are incomplete. As far as consensus behavior, see this: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3675#block-structure That defines ommersHash (uncleHash), difficulty, mixHash, nonce, and ommers (uncles) in consensus data structures post merge. I have considered that this is the spec: <https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/apis/json-rpc/> That is "useful documentation". 😄 Also note https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4399#block-structure which defines the field previously called `mixHash` as RANDAO in the block header. There is also https://ethereum.github.io/execution-apis/api-documentation/
